A man who recited a verse differently is brought to the Prophet, who says both readings are right and warns that nations before them differed and perished.
Umar brings Hisham to the Prophet for reciting Surat al-Furqan differently; the Prophet approves both readings, saying the Quran was revealed in seven ways.
Hearing a man recite in the mosque, the Prophet asked mercy for him for recalling verses he had dropped, and asked mercy for Abbad on recognising his voice.
The Prophet recited the verse 'Fahal min Muddakir' in the usual way.
Abdullah heard the Prophet recite 'Fahal min Muddakir'.
The Prophet recited the verse 'Hal min Muddakir', is there any that will remember.
Two men recited a verse differently; displeased at their dispute, the Prophet said both were correct and they should not differ, for nations before them differed and were destroyed.
A cloud hovered over a man reciting Surat al-Kahf as his animal took fright, and the Prophet said it was peace descending for the recitation of the Quran.
Ibn Mas'ud has Alqama recite fifty verses of Surat Maryam, which Khabbab praises, then tells Khabbab to throw away his gold ring, and he does.
Al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses, is the greatest surah of the Quran, and whoever says Ameen when the imam ends it, in time with the angels, is forgiven.
Ibn Masud recited An-Nisa to the Prophet, who liked hearing the Quran from others; at the verse on a witness from each nation he stopped him, eyes overflowing with tears.
The Prophet told Abu Sa'id the call of Allah and His Apostle must be answered even in prayer, and named Al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses, the greatest sura.
Ibn Masud recited 'Haita laka' and said they recite it as they were taught it.
The Prophet named Al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses, the greatest sura and the substance of the Quran, after asking Abu Sa'id why he had not answered his call.
Ibn Masud said the suras Bani Israel, Al-Kahf and Maryam are among his first old treasures.
Abdullah says Bani Israel, Al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha and Al-Anbiya are among the very old surahs he learnt by heart, his first property.
On the day of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath in a vibrating, pleasant voice.
A companion's horse kept jumping while he recited the Quran, and the Prophet said it was tranquillity descending because of the recitation.
Hearing the Prophet recite Surat at-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, Jubair's heart nearly flew at the verses asking whether they were created by nothing or are the creators.
The Prophet recited 'Fahal min Muddakir' with a d, and corrected Abdullah when he recited it with dh.
One who recites the Quran and knows it by heart will be with the noble scribes, and one who learns it with great difficulty gets a double reward.
Abu Ad-Darda' confirms Alqama's reading 'By the male and the female', as heard from Ibn Mas'ud and from the Prophet, refusing the reading others want.
Gabriel recited the Quran to the Prophet in seven ways, and when Umar objects to Hisham's different reading of al-Furqan, the Prophet says both were revealed so.
Gabriel met the Prophet every night of Ramadan to go over the Quran, once a year and twice in the year he died, when he stayed twenty days in Itikaf.
Al-Fatiha is the most superior surah and cured a chief stung by a scorpion, and reciting the last two verses of al-Baqarah at night is sufficient.
Tranquillity and angels descended on reciters of al-Kahf and al-Baqarah; the Prophet loved al-Fath; al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Quran; he recited the refuge surahs and blew over himself.
Allah listens to no prophet as He listens to one who recites the Quran aloud in a pleasant tone.
The best of the Muslims are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
Keep reciting the Quran, which escapes faster than tied camels, and do not say 'I forgot'; the Prophet recited al-Fath riding, and Ibn Abbas learnt the Mufassal as a boy.
A reciter reminds the Prophet of missed verses; saying 'I forgot' is disliked, the Quran was revealed in several readings, and reciting the Mufassal in a day is too quick.
The Prophet prolonged sounds when reciting and recited al-Fath softly in a vibrating tone on his camel; he tells Abu Musa he has a melodious voice like David's family.
The Prophet likes hearing the Quran from others and weeps as Ibn Mas'ud recites an-Nisa; Ibn Shubruma holds three verses the least to recite, and al-Baqarah's last two suffice.
Abdullah bin Amr, fasting daily and finishing the Quran nightly, is told to finish it in a month, then no less than seven days; the Prophet weeps hearing Ibn Mas'ud.
Recite the Quran while agreeing on its meaning and stop when you differ; the Prophet tells two men reciting differently both are correct, and says earlier nations perished by differing.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a citron, one not reciting like a date; a hypocrite reciting is like a fragrant bitter plant, one not reciting like colocynth.
Abu Ad-Darda' asked Alqama of Kufa about its distinguished companions and how Ibn Mas'ud recited Sura 92, upholding 'and by male and female' as heard from the Prophet.
When a man thought repeating Surat al-Ikhlas alone was too little, the Prophet swore that it equals one third of the Quran.
Umar dragged Hisham to the Prophet for reciting Surat al-Furqan differently; the Prophet approved both readings, saying the Quran was revealed to be recited in seven ways.
The Prophet said to recite the Quran while hearts agree on its meaning and to stop reading when people differ over it.
The surah 'He is Allah, the One' equals a third of the Quran, and a man who loved reciting it for describing the Beneficent was told Allah loves him.
The Prophet asked a man whether he knew anything of the Quran, and he named the surahs he knew.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to the Prophet reciting the Quran aloud in a pleasant voice.
The verse forbidding prayer too loud or too low came while the Prophet hid in Mecca: recite so companions hear, but not pagans, who abused the Quran.
Whoever does not recite the Quran in a pleasing voice is not one of us, which others explained as reciting it aloud.
On the day of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath on his camel in a vibrating, pleasant voice, which the narrators later imitated.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to a Prophet reciting the Quran in an attractive, audible, sweet voice.
Al-Bara' never heard a better voice than the Prophet's reciting At-Tin in the Isha prayer; hiding in Mecca, he was told to recite neither too loud nor too low.
The Prophet recited the Quran with his head in Aisha's lap while she menstruated, and told Umar and Hisham, reciting differently, that the Quran was revealed in seven ways.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a fragrant, tasty citron, one not reciting like a date; an impious reciter is like a fragrant bitter herb, a non-reciter like colocynth.
